explanation: Phylum Zygomycota contains fungi that are mainly saprotrophs, decomposing animal and plant matter. They are commonly found on baked goods. A prominent example is the black bread mold (Rhizopus stolonifer), which has both asexual and sexual life cycles. Its spores settle on food and develop into three types of specialized hyphae: 1) Stolons, which grow horizontally across the surface of the bread; 2) Rhizoids, which grow downward into the bread as anchors; and 3) Sporangiophores, which are aerial hyphae that produce haploid spores.
